source.title: pbSGD: Powered Stochastic Gradient Descent Methods for Accelerated Non-Convex Optimization
source.authors: Beitong Zhou; Jun Liu; Wei-Gao Sun; Ru-Fu Chen; C. Tomlin; Ye Yuan

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer and batch-size conditions and reports held-out image-classification performance using its own experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and a batch-size sweep relevant to V4 and V5. The cited claims about adaptive optimizers and large batches in prior work are not treated as this paper’s results. Training-accuracy curves are not separately extracted where the text gives no usable numeric result.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adaptive-optimizer versus SGDM test-accuracy comparisons relevant to V4, and an SGD versus pbSGD batch-size sweep relevant to V5. It is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the empirical generalization findings. The authors also conclude that powered gradients accelerate initial training, improve hyperparameter robustness, mitigate vanishing gradients, and complement learning-rate schedules; their theoretical convergence bounds match existing SGD and SGDM rates.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a powered-gradient optimizer with SGDM and adaptive optimizers; experiments tune learning rates and the power exponent, use scheduled learning-rate reductions in the main comparisons, and use fixed learning rates in the batch-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer choice affects test accuracy; batch size affects SGD test accuracy, while pbSGD is reported as more stable. Learning-rate schedule and power exponent also vary in reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: pbSGD and pbSGDM achieve slightly lower test accuracy than SGDM in the recorded CIFAR comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Powered-gradient optimizers can approach momentum SGD's image-classification accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-20)
record.problems: The authors report averages over at least five random initializations but provide no uncertainty estimates. Most optimizer results are described for a small set of image-classification experiments; the batch-size sweep is figure-only, without exact values in the text. The paper reports test accuracy rather than a direct numerical training-to-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Figure-only values for the batch-size sweep are retained with values recorded as figure only.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width dependence beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local-connectivity interventions.

Language benchmarks, broader tuning of optimizer parameters, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. Equal or better final training performance is not numerically established by the extracted rows.
Language models, longer-training interventions, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization or regularization changes in the batch-size sweep.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Additional adaptive baselines: ResNet-50/CIFAR-10 has AdaGrad 91.87% and RMSprop 92.99%, versus SGDM 94.75%; WideResNet/CIFAR-100 has AdaGrad 74.05% and RMSprop 73.71%, versus SGDM 76.78%. These comparisons are omitted despite the declaration that no eligible results were omitted.
DenseNet-121/CIFAR-10 best test accuracies: SGDM 95.07%, Adam 93.57%, AdaGrad 92.16%, RMSprop 93.43%. Add linked comparator and adaptive-method rows.
ResNeXt-29/CIFAR-100 best test accuracies: SGDM 79.12%, Adam 77.06%, AdaGrad 75.89%, RMSprop 76.84%. Add linked comparator and adaptive-method rows.
ResNet-50/ImageNet best test accuracies: SGDM 76.27%, Adam 72.71%, AdaGrad 68.98%, RMSprop 72.44%, with batch size 256, 120 epochs, and tenfold learning-rate reductions every 30 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope label based solely on missing train–test-gap measurements or limited dataset coverage: these are untested aspects, not demonstrated failures. Results are averages over at least five random initializations without reported uncertainty. Hyperparameter selection used the test set, so the reported test accuracies also served as selection criteria.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Language benchmarks; broader optimizer tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Language models; fixed epoch-budget comparisons; recipe changes involving warmup, normalization, or regularization.
Sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring retrained test accuracy.
